content:
Hello!

I'm currently interning at JetBrains, working on formalization for the Kotlin programming language. as part of my internship, i wrote a framework for specifying and verifying dataflow analyses, which means I formalized a relatively simple theory of lattices, CFGs, and wrote a mechanized version of Kildall's algorithm with proofs of termination and correctness (correct computation of a (least-)postfixpoint). You can find the source for the framework here; it is defined in the Analysis/ directory.

I think the implementation of the algorithm is generic enough to be of theoretical interest, and we are available to update or change any definition to fit CSLib's style. In particular, we wrote our own lattices to remove any dependency on Mathlib, but adapting to Mathlib would not be too hard.

Would this be something of interest to merge into CSLib? Are we stepping on anyone's feet?

You are welcomed to contribute. Please read CSLib's policy regarding contribution, especially regarding AI:
https://github.com/ctchou/cslib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
Please split your contribution into reasonably sized chunks, in order to facilitate reviews. Yes, you should use Mathlib as much as possible.
